cards.title: Polynomial-time, polynomial-factor approximation of Euclidean SVP
cards.formal: Is there a constant C and a classical polynomial-time algorithm that, given a rank-n rational lattice basis, returns a nonzero lattice vector of Euclidean length at most n^C λ1(L)?
cards.context:
Classical search SVP in the Euclidean norm. A hardness result at a smaller polynomial approximation factor does not rule out an algorithm at a larger one.

TCS-0655 asks to rule out n^ε-GapSVP under a standard assumption for SOME small ε; this is not equivalent to finding a vector within n^C for SOME possibly large C. cards.why: Asks whether Euclidean shortest vectors can be approximated within any fixed polynomial factor in polynomial time, a central gap between lattice algorithms and cryptographic assumptions.

cards.formal: Does every finite graph satisfy χ(G)≤ceil((Δ(G)+1+ω(G))/2), where χ is chromatic number, Δ maximum degree and ω maximum clique size?

cards.title: The optimal quantitative Excluded Grid Theorem
cards.formal: Let f(r) be the least treewidth threshold forcing an r×r grid minor in every graph. Is f(r)=O(r² polylog r), and what is its tight asymptotic order?
cards.context:
The target is the optimal order, not a modest exponent improvement. Do not claim O(r²): the known lower bound includes log r. The cited literature records competing near-quadratic and cubic conjectures; the universally agreed open target is the tight threshold, not a consensus on the answer.

TCS-4404 concerns a cylindrical/directed grid question. TCS-5475 concerns parameters in the graph-minor STRUCTURE theorem; it is not the treewidth threshold for an undirected grid minor.
cards.why: A foundational quantitative question in graph minor theory, controlling grid obstructions to small treewidth and their algorithmic applications.

cards.title: The computational Kesten–Stigum threshold for sparse community recovery
cards.formal: In the balanced symmetric sparse stochastic block model with a fixed q≥5 groups and edge probabilities a/n within groups and b/n between groups (a>b>0), can any polynomial-time algorithm achieve nonvanishing correlation with the planted labels below (a−b)²=q(a+(q−1)b), in the regime where recovery is information-theoretically possible?
cards.context:
The 2025 result is conditional on the extended low-degree conjecture. The proposed unrestricted polynomial-time barrier is not a proved theorem.

TCS-5248 addresses bipartite SBM spectral algorithms; TCS-5744 addresses SDP/Bayes-error behavior. Prior planted clique and tensor PCA concern other planted models. TCS-1187 is the distinct growing-number-of-communities regime q>sqrt(n), whereas this target fixes q.
cards.why: A canonical statistical-versus-computational gap: whether the Kesten–Stigum threshold is the true efficient-recovery barrier for sparse communities.
